problemStatement.plain: Formalize the first moment method: if E[X] > t then some outcome exceeds t, with applications to Ramsey lower bounds.

proven: The first moment principle is formalized for finite averages: if the average is above a threshold, some element exceeds that threshold.
The dual first moment form and finite pigeonhole variants are proved.
Linearity of expectation is represented through Finset.sum_add_distrib.
A Ramsey lower-bound existence statement is included in the formalized workflow.
The associated Lean files are recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: This entry is scoped to the finite first-moment workflow, not a broad probability library.
Further probabilistic-method applications remain separate extensions.
knownResults.goal: Use the completed finite first-moment formalization as the base probabilistic-method building block.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: 0 sorries, 0 axioms. First moment principle, linearity of expectation, Ramsey lower bound existence, plus additional lemmas (dual, pigeonhole variants).

first_moment_dual: if avg < t then ∃ element < t
